title: Events, Diagnostics & Introspection
intro: Beyond logs and describe, kubectl has tools for seeing the raw event stream and looking up what any resource type/field actually means.

steps.prompt: See the most recent cluster events, oldest first.
steps.fake_output:
LAST SEEN   TYPE      REASON        OBJECT       MESSAGE
5m          Warning   BackOff       pod/web-abc  Back-off restarting failed container
1m          Normal    Scheduled     pod/db-1     Successfully assigned
steps.explanation: Plain 'kubectl get events' isn't sorted by default and can be confusing — this flag puts them in actual chronological order.
steps.why: You could also filter to one object specifically with --field-selector=involvedObject.name=<pod>, which is better once you know exactly what you're investigating rather than scanning everything.

steps.prompt: You don't remember every field a Pod spec supports — look it up.
steps.fake_output:
KIND: Pod
VERSION: v1

FIELD: spec <PodSpec>

DESCRIPTION:
  Specification of the desired behavior of the pod.
  containers, volumes, nodeSelector, restartPolicy, ...
steps.explanation: 'explain' pulls field documentation straight from the API server — no need to leave the terminal or guess at YAML structure.
steps.why: This beats searching the web for k8s API docs since it's guaranteed to match the exact API version your actual cluster is running, not just whatever version a search result happens to describe.

steps.prompt: Extract just the phase of pod 'web-abc' directly, without eyeballing full output.
steps.explanation: jsonpath pulls exactly one field out of the object — useful for scripting instead of parsing describe's human-readable text.
steps.why: 'kubectl get pod web-abc -o yaml' has this too, but jsonpath returns ONLY the value you asked for — much easier to use inside a shell script's if-statement.

steps.prompt: See which API resource types exist in this cluster (useful when you're not sure of a resource's short name).
steps.fake_output:
NAME          SHORTNAMES   APIVERSION   NAMESPACED   KIND
pods          po           v1           true         Pod
deployments   deploy       apps/v1      true         Deployment
steps.explanation: This is the master list every short name (po, deploy, svc...) you've been using throughout these tutorials actually comes from.
steps.why: This is the fastest way to discover a resource type's exact name/shortname/API group when you're working with something less common than pods or deployments, instead of guessing or searching docs.
